correctness.rationale: The zero-center minimum-ball certificate follows by averaging the squared distances of a farthest point and its antipode. The signed vertex norm reduces to a positive-weight cyclic Ising cost with even-product parity, giving the radius formula and all contacts for every n>=4. For fixed total edge weight, Cauchy--Schwarz gives all even optimizers. In odd order, averaging the n single-defect norm forms and Fourier diagonalization of the cyclic shift produces a strictly positive quadratic lower bound, proves uniqueness at equal weights and the stated stability constant. The separately executable exact checker reproduces 3360 finite sign-pattern configurations but is not used for the infinite argument.

value.rationale: For triangle-free cycles, independent positive edge-generator weights are a full natural deformation family. Fixing their sum fixes total Euclidean generator length and makes a well-motivated geometric resource comparison. The result solves the exact outer-sphere problem and all contacts for every weight choice, identifies a nonobvious parity distinction in the entire continuous minimizer locus (odd rigid, even one-parameter), and quantitatively bounds odd-cycle nonuniformity. This complete family classification is not a random narrow parameter slice or a numerical table.
